sentences.chinese: 陳訓
sentences.literal: Chen Xun.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Xun

sentences.chinese: 陳訓，字道元，曆陽人。
sentences.literal: Chen Xun, style name Daoyuan, was a man of Liyang.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Xun, courtesy name Daoyuan, came from Liyang.

sentences.chinese: 少好秘學，天文、算曆、陰陽、占候無不畢綜，尤善風角。
sentences.literal: In youth he loved occult learning; in astronomy, calendrical calculation, yin-yang, and prognostication by signs there was none he did not master comprehensively, and he was especially skilled in fengjiao.
sentences.idiomatic: As a youth he devoured esoteric studies—astronomy, calendar math, yin-yang, and omen-reading—and excelled above all at wind-angle divination.

sentences.chinese: 孫晧以為奉禁都尉，使其占侯。
sentences.literal: Sun Hao appointed him Attendant Commandant of the Forbidden Palaces and had him perform prognostications.
sentences.idiomatic: The last Wu emperor Sun Hao named him palace attendant for forbidden precincts and set him to read the omens.

sentences.chinese: 晧政嚴酷，訓知其必敗而不敢言。
sentences.literal: Hao's government was harsh and cruel; Xun knew he was bound to fail yet dared not speak.
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Hao ruled with terror; Chen Xun saw the dynasty was doomed but kept silent.

sentences.chinese: 時錢唐湖開，或言天下當太平，青蓋入洛陽。
sentences.literal: At that time the Qiantang Lake opened; some said the realm would soon be at peace and the "green canopy" would enter Luoyang.
sentences.idiomatic: When Qiantang Lake burst its banks, court gossip took it for an omen of universal peace and the Wu ruler's green-canopy carriage arriving in Luoyang.

sentences.chinese: 晧以問訓，訓曰：「臣止能望氣，不能達湖之開塞。
sentences.literal: Hao asked Xun about it; Xun said, "Your servant can only observe qi; I cannot fathom whether the lake opens or closes.
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Hao pressed him; Chen Xun answered carefully that he could read vapors, not hydraulics.

sentences.chinese: 」退而告其友曰：「青蓋入洛，將有輿櫬銜璧之事，非吉祥也。
sentences.literal: " Withdrawing, he told his friend, "When the green canopy enters Luo, there will be affairs of a bier borne forth and jade held in the mouth—it is not auspicious.
sentences.idiomatic: Privately he warned a friend that "green canopy to Luoyang" foretold a funeral surrender, not fortune.

sentences.chinese: 」尋而吳亡。
sentences.literal: " Soon thereafter Wu perished.
sentences.idiomatic: Wu fell almost immediately afterward.

sentences.chinese: 訓隨例內徙，拜諫義大夫。
sentences.literal: Xun moved inward with the general migration and was appointed Grandee of Remonstrance.
sentences.idiomatic: He relocated with the other southern households and received the remonstrance grandee's title.

sentences.chinese: 俄而去職還鄉。
sentences.literal: Before long he left office and returned to his home district.
sentences.idiomatic: He soon resigned and went home to Liyang.

sentences.chinese: 及陳敏作亂，遣弟宏為曆陽太守，訓謂邑人曰：「陳家無王氣，不久當滅。
sentences.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, sending his younger brother Hong as governor of Liyang, Xun told the townspeople, "The Chen clan lacks kingly qi; before long they will be destroyed.
sentences.idiomatic: When Chen Min rose and installed his brother Chen Hong at Liyang, Chen Xun told neighbors the Chen house carried no imperial aura and would collapse soon.

sentences.chinese: 」宏聞，將斬之。
sentences.literal: " Hong heard of it and was about to execute him.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Hong planned to kill him for the remark.

sentences.chinese: 訓鄉人秦琚為宏參軍，乃說訓曰：「訓善風角，可試之。
sentences.literal: Xun's fellow townsman Qin Ju served Hong as army aide and therefore urged Xun, saying, "Xun is skilled in fengjiao—put him to the test.
sentences.idiomatic: Army adviser Qin Ju, a townsman, begged Chen Hong to try Chen Xun's wind-angle art before shedding blood.

sentences.chinese: 如不中，徐斬未晚也。
sentences.literal: If he misses, you may behead him slowly—it will not be late."
sentences.idiomatic: If his reading failed, they could execute him at leisure.

sentences.chinese: 」乃赦之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he was spared.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Hong stayed the blade.

sentences.chinese: 時宏攻征東參軍衡彥于曆陽，乃問訓曰：「城中有幾千人？
sentences.literal: At that time Hong was attacking Eastern Campaign Army aide Heng Yan at Liyang; he therefore asked Xun, "How many men are in the city?
sentences.idiomatic: While Chen Hong besieged Eastern Campaign aide Heng Yan in Liyang, he demanded to know the garrison's strength.

sentences.chinese: 攻之可拔不？
sentences.literal: Can it be taken by assault?"
sentences.idiomatic: He asked whether the walls could be stormed.

sentences.chinese: 」訓登牛渚山望氣，曰：「不過五百人。
sentences.literal: " Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu to observe qi and said, "Not more than five hundred.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu, read the vapors, and put the defenders under five hundred.

sentences.chinese: 然不可攻，攻之必敗。
sentences.literal: Yet you must not attack; if you attack, you will surely be defeated."
sentences.idiomatic: He forbade an assault anyway, warning that any attack would fail.

sentences.chinese: 」宏復大怒曰：「何有五千人攻五百人而有不得理？
sentences.literal: " Hong raged again, saying, "How can five thousand men attack five hundred and lack reason to prevail?"
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Hong fumed that five thousand ought to overrun five hundred.

sentences.chinese: 」命將士攻之，果為彥所敗，方信訓有道術，乃優遇之。
sentences.literal: " He ordered his generals and soldiers to attack; they were indeed defeated by Yan; only then did he believe Xun possessed the way of techniques and treated him generously.
sentences.idiomatic: The storming host was routed by Heng Yan; chastened, Chen Hong honored Chen Xun as a true adept.

sentences.chinese: 都水參軍淮南周亢嘗問訓以官位，訓曰：「君至卯年當剖符近郡，酉年當有曲蓋。
sentences.literal: Army Waterways aide Zhou Kang of Huainan once asked Xun about office rank; Xun said, "By the mao year you ought to split tallies for a nearby commandery; by the you year you ought to receive a bent canopy."
sentences.idiomatic: Zhou Kang of Huainan, an aide on waterworks, asked his career; Chen Xun promised a nearby governorship in a mao year and a bent-canopy general's train in a you year.

sentences.chinese: 」亢曰：「脫如來言，當相薦拔。
sentences.literal: " Kang said, "If it comes as you say, I shall recommend and promote you."
sentences.idiomatic: Zhou Kang vowed to pull strings if the prophecy held.

sentences.chinese: 」訓曰：「性不好官，惟欲得米耳。
sentences.literal: " Xun said, "By nature I dislike office—I only wish to obtain rice."
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Xun said he wanted grain, not promotion.

sentences.chinese: 」後亢果為義興太守、金紫將軍。
sentences.literal: " Later Kang indeed became governor of Yixing and general with gold ribbon and purple sash.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhou Kang later became Yixing governor and a gold-and-purple general, just as foretold.

sentences.chinese: 時劉聰、王彌寇洛陽，曆陽太守武瑕問訓曰：「國家人事如何？
sentences.literal: At that time Liu Cong and Wang Mi raided Luoyang; Wuxia, governor of Liyang, asked Xun, "How stand the court and the realm?"
sentences.idiomatic: When Liu Cong and Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Liyang governor Wu Xia asked Chen Xun for the fate of the Jin house.

sentences.chinese: 」訓曰：「胡賊三逼，國家當敗，天子野死。
sentences.literal: " Xun said, "Hu bandits press thrice; the state will be defeated and the Son of Heaven will die in the open wilds.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Xun said Xiongnu armies would thrice corner the throne, the dynasty would fall, and the emperor would perish in the field.

sentences.chinese: 今尚未也。
sentences.literal: Not yet now."
sentences.idiomatic: The worst had not arrived yet.

sentences.chinese: 」其後懷湣二帝果有平陽之酷焉。
sentences.literal: " Thereafter the two emperors Huai and Min indeed suffered the cruelty at Pingyang.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperors Huai and Min later endured captivity and murder at Pingyang, as he had warned.

sentences.chinese: 或問其以明年吉凶者，訓曰：「揚州刺史當死，武昌大火，上方節將亦當死。
sentences.literal: Someone asked him about the next year's good or ill; Xun said, "The Yangzhou governor will die; there will be a great fire in Wuchang; a general of the upper ranks will also die."
sentences.idiomatic: Asked about the coming year, he predicted the Yangzhou governor's death, a conflagration at Wuchang, and the passing of a senior commander.

sentences.chinese: 」至時，劉陶、周訪皆卒，武昌大火，燒數千家。
sentences.literal: " When the time came, Liu Tao and Zhou Fang both died; there was a great fire in Wuchang that burned several thousand households.
sentences.idiomatic: Liu Tao and Zhou Fang died on schedule, and Wuchang blazed through thousands of homes.

sentences.chinese: 時甘卓為曆陽太守，訓私謂所親曰：「甘侯頭低而視仰，相法名為眄刀，又目有赤脈，自外而入，不出十年，必以兵死，不領兵則可以免。
sentences.literal: At that time Gan Zhuo was governor of Liyang; Xun privately told those close to him, "Lord Gan's head hangs low while his gaze looks upward—in physiognomy this is called 'knife-squint'; moreover there are red threads in the eyes coming from without; within ten years he is sure to die by arms—if he does not command troops he may escape."
sentences.idiomatic: Watching Gan Zhuo at Liyang, Chen Xun whispered that his low head and upturned eyes formed the lethal "knife-squint" look, laced with red veins—within a decade steel would find him unless he shed command.

sentences.chinese: 」卓果為王敦所害。
sentences.literal: " Zhuo was indeed killed by Wang Dun.
sentences.idiomatic: Gan Zhuo fell to Wang Dun's coup, sword in hand.

sentences.chinese: 丞相王導多病，每自憂慮，以問訓。
sentences.literal: Chancellor Wang Dao was often ill and each time worried himself; he asked Xun about it.
sentences.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Dao, chronically unwell, consulted Chen Xun in his anxiety.

sentences.chinese: 訓曰：「公耳豎垂肩，必壽，亦大貴，子孫當興于江東。
sentences.literal: Xun said, "Your ears hang straight to the shoulders—you must enjoy long life, and you are also greatly noble; descendants will rise east of the Yangzi."
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Xun read his pendulous ears as signs of long life, high rank, and a flourishing lineage in Jiangdong.

sentences.chinese: 」咸如其言。
sentences.literal: " In every case it happened as he said.
sentences.idiomatic: Each prediction proved true.

sentences.chinese: 訓年八十餘卒。
sentences.literal: Xun died in his eighties.
sentences.idiomatic: He died past eighty.

sentences.chinese: 戴洋
sentences.literal: Dai Yang.
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang

sentences.chinese: 戴洋，字國流，吳興長城人也。
sentences.literal: Dai Yang, style name Guoliu, was a man of Changcheng in Wuxing.
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang, courtesy name Guoliu, was a native of Changcheng in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.chinese: 年十二，遇病死，五日而蘇。
sentences.literal: At age twelve he fell ill and died, and after five days revived.
sentences.idiomatic: At twelve he sickened, "died," and woke again after five days.

sentences.chinese: 說死時天使其為酒藏吏，授符錄，給吏從幡麾，將上蓬萊、昆侖、積石、太室、恆、廬、衡等諸山。
sentences.literal: He said that when dead Heaven had made him a clerk of the wine vaults, handed him tallies and registers, given him clerks with banners and standards, and was about to take him up Mount Penglai, Kunlun, Jishi, Taishi, Heng, Lu, Heng, and the other various mountains.
sentences.idiomatic: He described a posthumous posting as celestial cellar-keeper with registers, escorts, and a tour of the sacred peaks from Penglai to the great Heng ranges.

sentences.chinese: 既而遣歸，逢一老父，謂之曰：「汝後當得道，為貴人所識。
sentences.literal: Then he was sent back; meeting an old man, the man told him, "Later you will obtain the Way and be recognized by noble men."
sentences.idiomatic: Sent back to life, an elder promised he would win the Dao and earn patronage from the mighty.

sentences.chinese: 」及長，遂善風角。
sentences.literal: " When he grew up, he was skilled at fengjiao.
sentences.idiomatic: As an adult he mastered wind-angle divination.

sentences.chinese: 為人短陋，無風望，然好道術，妙解占侯卜數。
sentences.literal: As a man he was short and plain in appearance, lacking an imposing air, yet he loved techniques of the Way and marvelously understood prognostication, divination, and numerology.
sentences.idiomatic: He was homely and slight, yet obsessed with occult arts and uncannily sharp at omens, oracles, and fate reckoning.

sentences.chinese: 吳末為台吏，知吳將亡，託病不仕。
sentences.literal: At the end of Wu he was a Secretariat clerk; knowing Wu would perish, he pleaded illness and did not take office.
sentences.idiomatic: Late in Wu he held a clerkship at headquarters, saw the kingdom's end coming, and feigned illness to stay out of service.

sentences.chinese: 及吳平，還鄉里。
sentences.literal: When Wu was pacified, he returned to his home village.
sentences.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu he went home.

sentences.chinese: 後行至瀨鄉，經老子祠，皆是洋昔死時所見使處，但不復見昔物耳。
sentences.literal: Later, traveling, he came to Lai township and passed the shrine to Laozi—all were places Dai Yang had been made to serve when dead, yet he no longer saw the former things.
sentences.idiomatic: Passing Laozi's shrine at Lai township, he recognized every corner from his otherworldly errand, though the spirit furnishings had vanished.

sentences.chinese: 因問守藏應鳳曰：「去二十餘年，嘗有人乘馬東行，過老君而不下馬，未達橋，墜馬死者不？
sentences.literal: Therefore he asked the vault-keeper Ying Feng, "More than twenty years ago, was there one who rode a horse east, passed Lord Lao without dismounting, and before reaching the bridge fell from his horse and died?"
sentences.idiomatic: He asked keeper Ying Feng whether a rider had once insulted the god by staying mounted and died before the bridge—twenty years past.

sentences.chinese: 」鳳言有之。
sentences.literal: " Feng said there was.
sentences.idiomatic: Ying Feng confirmed the tale.

sentences.chinese: 所問之事，多與洋同。
sentences.literal: The matters he asked about mostly matched what Yang had seen.
sentences.idiomatic: Every detail matched Dai Yang's infernal itinerary.

sentences.chinese: 揚州刺史嘗問吉凶於洋，答曰：「熒惑入南斗，八月有暴水，九月當有客軍西南來。
sentences.literal: The Yangzhou governor once asked Dai Yang about good or ill; he answered, "Mars has entered the Southern Dipper—in the eighth month there will be violent flooding; in the ninth month there ought to be a guest army from the southwest."
sentences.idiomatic: Consulted by the Yangzhou governor, he warned of Mars in the Dipper—cloudbursts in the eighth month and an alien column from the southwest in the ninth.

sentences.chinese: 」如期果大水，而石冰作亂。
sentences.literal: " On schedule there was indeed great flooding, and Shi Bing rose in rebellion.
sentences.idiomatic: The floods came on time, and Shi Bing's revolt followed.

sentences.chinese: 冰既據揚州，洋謂人曰：「視賊雲氣，四月當破。
sentences.literal: After Bing had seized Yangzhou, Dai Yang told people, "Observing the bandits' cloud-qi, in the fourth month they will be broken."
sentences.idiomatic: Once Shi Bing held Yangzhou, Dai Yang read his banners and gave him until the fourth month to collapse.

sentences.chinese: 」果如其言。
sentences.literal: " It happened as he said.
sentences.idiomatic: The rebellion fell in that month.

sentences.chinese: 時陳敏為右將軍，堂邑令孫混見而羨之。
sentences.literal: At that time Chen Min was General of the Right; Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi, saw him and envied him.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Min, General of the Right, drew envious stares from Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi.

sentences.chinese: 洋曰：「敏當作賊族滅，何足願也！
sentences.literal: Dai Yang said, "Min will rebel and his clan be exterminated—what is there to envy!"
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang snapped that Chen Min would turn traitor and wipe his own line—hardly a model to covet.

sentences.chinese: 」未幾，敏果反而誅焉。
sentences.literal: " Before long Min indeed rebelled and was executed.
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Min revolted and died under the blade almost at once.

sentences.chinese: 初，混欲迎其家累，洋曰：「此地當敗，得臘不得正，豈可移家於賊中乎！
sentences.literal: At first Hun wished to bring his family dependents; Dai Yang said, "This place is about to fall—you may reach the year-end sacrifice month but not the first month—how can you move a household into the midst of bandits!"
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Hun meant to fetch his kin; Dai Yang swore the town would fall after la but before the new year and forbade dragging families into a war zone.

sentences.chinese: 」混便止。
sentences.literal: " Hun then desisted.
sentences.idiomatic: Sun Hun stayed put.

sentences.chinese: 歲末，敏弟昶攻堂邑，混遂以單身走免。
sentences.literal: At year's end Min's younger brother Chang attacked Tangyi, and Hun therefore fled alone and escaped.
sentences.idiomatic: When Chen Min's brother Chen Chang stormed Tangyi at year's end, Sun Hun slipped away alone.

sentences.chinese: 其後都水馬武舉洋為都水令史，洋請急還鄉。
sentences.literal: Thereafter Director of Waters Ma Wu recommended Dai Yang as clerk to the Director of Waters; Dai Yang requested emergency leave to return home.
sentences.idiomatic: Ma Wu of the waterways directorate named him a waterways clerk; Dai Yang begged leave and hurried home.

sentences.chinese: 將赴洛，夢神人謂之曰：「洛中當敗，人盡南渡，後五年揚州必有天子。
sentences.literal: About to go to Luoyang, he dreamed a spirit told him, "Luoyang is about to collapse; the people will all cross south; after five years Yangzhou is sure to have a Son of Heaven."
sentences.idiomatic: Bound for Luoyang, he dreamed a god warning of the capital's fall, a great southern flight, and an emperor in Yangzhou within five years.

sentences.chinese: 」洋信之，遂不去。
sentences.literal: " Dai Yang believed it and therefore did not go.
sentences.idiomatic: He canceled the journey and believed the vision.

sentences.chinese: 既而皆如其夢。
sentences.literal: Thereafter everything matched his dream.
sentences.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as the dream had said.

sentences.chinese: 廬江太守華譚問洋曰：「天下誰當復作賊者？
sentences.literal: Lujiang governor Hua Tan asked Dai Yang, "Who under Heaven is next likely to turn bandit?
sentences.idiomatic: Lujiang governor Hua Tan asked who in the realm would next rise in rebellion.

sentences.chinese: 」洋曰：「王機。
sentences.literal: " Dai Yang said, "Wang Ji."
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang answered, "Wang Ji."

sentences.chinese: 」尋而機反。
sentences.literal: " Soon thereafter Wang Ji indeed rebelled.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Ji revolted almost at once.

sentences.chinese: 陳眕問洋曰：「人言江南當有貴人，顧彥先、周宣珮當是不？
sentences.literal: Chen Zhen asked Dai Yang, "People say south of the Yangzi there will be an eminent man—might it be Gu Yanxian and Zhou Xuanpei?"
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Zhen asked whether Gu Rong and Zhou Pei were the great men fate had marked for the south.

sentences.chinese: 」洋曰：「顧不及臘，周不見來年八月。
sentences.literal: " Dai Yang said, "Gu will not reach the la month; Zhou will not see the eighth month of next year."
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang said Gu Rong would not live to la and Zhou Pei would die before the eighth month of the coming year.

sentences.chinese: 」榮果以十二月十七日卒，十九日臘，珮以明年七月晦亡。
sentences.literal: " Rong indeed died on the seventeenth day of the twelfth month; the la sacrifice fell on the nineteenth; Pei died on the last day of the seventh month the next year.
sentences.idiomatic: Gu Rong died on the seventeenth of the twelfth month, la came two days later, and Zhou Pei perished on the final day of the seventh month next year—each on schedule.

sentences.chinese: 王導遇病，召洋問之。
sentences.literal: Wang Dao fell ill and summoned Dai Yang.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Dao took sick and called Dai Yang to his bedside.

sentences.chinese: 洋曰：「君侯本命在申，金為土使之主，而于申上石頭立冶，火光照天，此為金火相爍，水火相煎，以故受害耳。
sentences.literal: Dai Yang said, "Your lordship's natal stem sits in shen; metal is earth's controlling agent, yet on shen above Stone Citadel they have set a smeltery—firelight shines to heaven; this is metal and fire scorching each other, water and fire seething each other—therefore you suffer harm."
sentences.idiomatic: He traced Wang Dao's fate to the shen stem, where a royal foundry atop Stone Citadel set metal and fire at war and poisoned the patron of earth.

sentences.chinese: 」導即移居東府，病遂差。
sentences.literal: " Dao immediately moved residence to the Eastern Bureau, and the illness then improved.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Dao relocated to the Eastern Secretariat compound and recovered.

sentences.chinese: 鎮東從事中郎張闓舉洋為丞相令史。
sentences.literal: Army aide to the General Who Guards the East Zhang Kai recommended Dai Yang as clerical secretary to the Chancellor.
sentences.idiomatic: Zhang Kai, staff officer to the general who guards the east, recommended him as a chancellery clerk.

sentences.chinese: 時司馬颺為烏程令，將赴職，洋曰：「君宜深慎下吏。
sentences.literal: At that time Sima Yang was magistrate of Wucheng and was about to take up the post; Dai Yang said, "You ought deeply to beware your subordinate clerks."
sentences.idiomatic: When Sima Yang left for his Wucheng magistracy, Dai Yang warned him to watch his underlings.

sentences.chinese: 」揚後果坐吏免官。
sentences.literal: " Yang later indeed lost office because of a clerk's crime.
sentences.idiomatic: Sima Yang was cashiered when a clerk's guilt touched him.

sentences.chinese: 洋又謂曰：「卿雖免官，十一月當作郡，加將軍。
sentences.literal: Dai Yang also told him, "Though you lose office, in the eleventh month you will become a governor and receive the title of general."
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang added that in the eleventh month he would govern a commandery with a general's commission.

sentences.chinese: 」至期，為太山太守、鎮武將軍。
sentences.literal: " When the term arrived, he became governor of Taishan and General Who Guards Martial Might.
sentences.idiomatic: On the date he was named Taishan governor and general who guards martial might.

sentences.chinese: 颺賣宅將行，洋止之曰：「君不得至，當還，不可無宅。
sentences.literal: Sima Yang sold his house and was about to depart; Dai Yang stopped him, saying, "You will not reach your post—you will return; you cannot be without a house."
sentences.idiomatic: As Sima Yang sold his house to leave, Dai Yang told him he would never reach Taishan and must keep a roof in the capital.

sentences.chinese: 」颺果為徐龕所逼，不得之郡。
sentences.literal: " Yang was indeed harried by Xu Kan and could not reach the commandery.
sentences.idiomatic: Xu Kan's revolt blocked his march and sent him home.

sentences.chinese: 元帝增颺眾二千，使助祖逖。
sentences.literal: Emperor Yuan added two thousand men to Yang's forces to assist Zu Ti.
sentences.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan bolstered Sima Yang with two thousand troops for Zu Ti's campaign.

sentences.chinese: 洋勸颺不行，颺乃稱疾。
sentences.literal: Dai Yang urged Yang not to go; Yang then pleaded illness.
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang begged him not to march; Sima Yang pleaded sickness instead.

sentences.chinese: 收付廷尉，俄而因赦得出。
sentences.literal: He was seized and delivered to the minister of justice; before long, thanks to an amnesty, he was released.
sentences.idiomatic: The court jailed him briefly until an amnesty freed him.

sentences.chinese: 元帝將登阼，使洋擇日，洋以為宜用三月二十四日丙午。
sentences.literal: When Emperor Yuan was about to ascend the throne, he had Dai Yang choose the day; Dai Yang held that the third month, twenty-fourth day, bingwu, ought to be used.
sentences.idiomatic: For Yuan-di's enthronement Dai Yang picked the bingwu day of the third month's twenty-fourth.

sentences.chinese: 太史令陳卓奏用二十二日，言：「昔越王用甲辰三月反國，范蠡稱在陽之前，當主盡出，上下盡空，德將出遊，刑入中宮，今與此同。
sentences.literal: Grand Astrologer Chen Zhuo memorialized to use the twenty-second day, saying, "In olden days the king of Yue used jiachen in the third month to return to his state; Fan Li said that while yang had not yet fully emerged, the host qi was utterly out and the upper and lower utterly empty, virtue was about to go forth on tour, and punishment entered the central palace—today matches that."
sentences.idiomatic: Chen Zhuo countered with the twenty-second, citing Yue's jiachen return and Fan Li's doctrine of empty hosts and wandering virtue.

sentences.chinese: 」洋曰：「越王為吳所囚，雖當時遜媚，實懷怨憤，蠡故用甲辰，乘德而歸，留刑吳宮。
sentences.literal: " Dai Yang said, "The king of Yue was imprisoned by Wu; though at the time he was submissive and ingratiating, in truth he harbored resentment and rage; Fan Li therefore used jiachen, riding virtue home while leaving punishment in Wu's palace.
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang replied that Goujian's calendar trick had humiliated a captor-king, not crowned a legitimate heir.

sentences.chinese: 今大王內無含咎，外無怨憤，當承天洪命，納祚無窮，何為追越王去國留殃故事邪！
sentences.literal: " Now the great king harbors no hidden fault within and bears no resentment without—he ought to receive Heaven's great mandate and take the blessing without end—why chase the precedent of the Yue king's leaving his state and leaving calamity behind!"
sentences.idiomatic: Yuan-di, he argued, was blameless and free of grudge—he should accept an auspicious enthronement date, not Yue's vengeful omen.

sentences.chinese: 」乃從之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon the court followed him.
sentences.idiomatic: The throne accepted Dai Yang's day.

sentences.chinese: 及祖約代兄鎮譙，請洋為中典軍，遷督護。
sentences.literal: When Zu Yue replaced his elder brother in garrisoning Qiao, he invited Dai Yang as Central Army aide and promoted him to superintendent.
sentences.idiomatic: When Zu Yue succeeded his brother on the Qiao front, he took Dai Yang as central-army adviser and raised him to superintendent.

sentences.chinese: 四月庚辰，禺中時有大風，起自東南，折木。
sentences.literal: On gengchen in the fourth month, at the yuzhong double-hour, there was a great wind rising from the southeast that broke trees.
sentences.idiomatic: On a fourth-month gengchen day, midmorning brought a southeast gale that snapped trees.

sentences.chinese: 洋謂約曰：「十月必有賊到譙城東，至曆陽，南方有反者。
sentences.literal: Dai Yang said to Yue, "In the tenth month bandits are sure to reach east of Qiao city as far as Liyang; south of that there will be rebels."
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang told Zu Yue that raiders would strike east of Qiao toward Liyang in the tenth month while the south also rose in revolt.

sentences.chinese: 」主簿王振以洋為妖，白約收洋，付刺奸而絕其食五十日，言語如故。
sentences.literal: " Registrar Wang Zhen, deeming Dai Yang a sorcerer, reported to Yue to seize Dai Yang; he was handed to the censorial jail and denied food for fifty days, yet his speech was as before.
sentences.idiomatic: Registrar Wang Zhen called it witchcraft and had him starved fifty days in the interrogation cells without breaking him.

sentences.chinese: 約知其有神術，乃赦之而讓振。
sentences.literal: Yue knew he possessed spirit-like techniques; thereupon he pardoned him and rebuked Zhen.
sentences.idiomatic: Zu Yue saw his power was real, freed him, and scolded Wang Zhen.

sentences.chinese: 振後有罪被收，洋救之。
sentences.literal: Later Zhen had a crime and was arrested; Dai Yang saved him.
sentences.idiomatic: When Wang Zhen later faced charges, Dai Yang interceded.

sentences.chinese: 約曰：「振往日相系，今何以救之？
sentences.literal: Yue said, "Zhen in former days bound you—why now save him?"
sentences.idiomatic: Zu Yue asked why he would rescue a man who had chained him.

sentences.chinese: 」洋曰：「振不識風角，非有宿嫌。
sentences.literal: " Dai Yang said, "Zhen did not understand fengjiao; there was no old grudge."
sentences.idiomatic: Dai Yang said Wang Zhen had acted from ignorance, not malice.

sentences.chinese: 振往時垂餓死，洋養活之，振猶尚遺忘。
sentences.literal: " At the time Zhen was on the verge of starving to death; Dai Yang fed and kept him alive, yet Zhen still afterward forgot.
sentences.idiomatic: He reminded Zu Yue that he had once fed Wang Zhen when the clerk was starving—a debt Wang Zhen forgot.

sentences.chinese: 夫處富貴而不棄貧賤甚難。
sentences.literal: " To dwell in wealth and honor yet not cast aside the poor and lowly is very difficult."
sentences.idiomatic: Few who sit in silk remember friends in rags.

sentences.chinese: 」約義之，即原振，賜洋米三十石。
sentences.literal: " Yue deemed this righteous; he immediately pardoned Zhen and granted Dai Yang thirty shi of rice.
sentences.idiomatic: Moved, Zu Yue spared Wang Zhen and paid Dai Yang thirty shi of grain.

sentences.chinese: 僕谷，劉曜胡位也。
sentences.literal: Pugu—Liu Yao's barbarian title.
sentences.idiomatic: Pugu was the Jie-style epithet for Liu Yao's rank.

sentences.chinese: 劬禿當，捉也。
sentences.literal: Qutu dang—capture.
sentences.idiomatic: The phrase qutu dang meant "to seize" or "to take captive."

sentences.chinese: 此言軍出捉得曜也。
sentences.literal: This saying is: the army goes forth and captures Yao.
sentences.idiomatic: Taken together, the oracle meant the host would march out and take Liu Yao alive.

sentences.chinese: 」又令一童子潔齋七日，取麻油合胭脂，躬自研於掌中，舉手示童子，粲然有輝。
sentences.literal: He further ordered one boy to purify in fast seven days, take sesame oil and mix rouge, personally grind it in his palm, raise his hand and show the boy—it blazed with radiance.
sentences.idiomatic: He had a novice fast seven days, blend sesame oil with rouge in his own palm, then lift his hand before the boy until it shone dazzling bright.

sentences.chinese: 童子驚曰：「有軍馬甚眾，見一人長大白晳，以硃絲縛其肘。
sentences.literal: The boy startled said, "There are very many troops and horses; I see one man, tall, large, fair and white, with vermilion silk binding his elbow.
sentences.idiomatic: The boy cried out that he saw endless squadrons and a towering, pale figure with crimson cords about his forearm.

sentences.chinese: 」澄曰：「此即曜也。
sentences.literal: " Cheng said, "This is Yao.
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng said, "That man is Liu Yao."

sentences.chinese: 」勒其悅，遂赴洛距曜，生擒之。
sentences.literal: " Le was greatly pleased; thereupon he hastened to Luoyang to oppose Yao and seized him alive.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le rejoiced, marched on Luoyang to meet Liu Yao, and took him prisoner alive.

sentences.chinese: 勒僭稱趙天王，行皇帝事，敬澄彌篤。
sentences.literal: Le usurped the title Heavenly King of Zhao and conducted the business of an emperor; his reverence for Cheng grew ever deeper.
sentences.idiomatic: Having arrogated the style Heavenly King of Zhao while wielding imperial power, Shi Le honored Fotucheng more devotedly than before.

sentences.chinese: 時石蔥將叛，澄誡勒曰：「今年蔥中有蟲，食必害人，可令百姓無食蔥也。
sentences.literal: At the time Shi Cong was about to rebel; Cheng admonished Le saying, "This year within cong there are worms—eating it will surely harm people; you may order the hundred surnames not to eat cong.
sentences.idiomatic: When Shi Cong plotted revolt, Fotucheng punned on the word "scallion" (cong) and warned Shi Le that "scallions" harbored worms—so the realm should shun them.

sentences.chinese: 」勒班告境內，慎無食蔥。
sentences.literal: " Le promulgated notice within the borders: be careful not to eat cong.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le issued an edict forbidding the people to touch scallions.

sentences.chinese: 俄而石蔥果走。
sentences.literal: Before long Shi Cong indeed fled.
sentences.idiomatic: Soon afterward Shi Cong bolted, as foretold.

sentences.chinese: 勒益重之，事必諮而後行，號曰大和尚。
sentences.literal: Le esteemed him the more; for affairs he invariably consulted him before acting, and styled him Great Monk.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le weighted him still higher, took counsel before every move, and addressed him as the Great Monk.

sentences.chinese: 勒愛子斌暴病死，將殯，勒歎曰：「朕聞虢太子死，扁鵲能生之，今可得效乎？
sentences.literal: Le's beloved son Bin died suddenly of illness; about to lay him out for burial, Le sighed, "We have heard that when the crown prince of Guo died, Bian Que could restore life—may we now obtain such efficacy?"
sentences.idiomatic: When his favorite son Shi Bin died suddenly on the eve of obsequies, Shi Le mourned aloud whether any healer could work Bian Que's miracle for the dead.

sentences.chinese: 」乃令告澄。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he ordered that Cheng be informed.
sentences.idiomatic: He sent word to Fotucheng.

sentences.chinese: 澄取楊枝沾水，灑而咒之。
sentences.literal: Cheng took a poplar twig, dipped it in water, sprinkled and chanted over him.
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng dipped a willow spray in water, sprinkled the corpse, and intoned spells.

sentences.chinese: 就執斌手曰：「可起矣！
sentences.literal: He went and grasped Bin's hand saying, "You may rise!"
sentences.idiomatic: He seized Shi Bin's hand and commanded him to rise.

sentences.chinese: 」因此遂蘇，有頃，平復。
sentences.literal: " From this he then revived; after a moment he was fully restored.
sentences.idiomatic: The prince stirred and within moments seemed wholly recovered.

sentences.chinese: 自是勒諸子多在澄寺中養之。
sentences.literal: From this Le's various sons for the most part were reared in Cheng's monastery.
sentences.idiomatic: Afterward most of Shi Le's sons were raised inside Fotucheng's temple.

sentences.chinese: 勒死之年，天靜無風，而塔上一鈴獨鳴，澄謂眾曰：「鈴音雲，國有大喪，不出今年矣。
sentences.literal: In the year Le died, heaven was still and without wind, yet on the pagoda one bell alone rang; Cheng told the assembly, "The bell's sound declares: the state has a great mourning—it will not extend beyond this year."
sentences.idiomatic: The year Shi Le died, though the air was breathless, a lone stupa bell tolled; Fotucheng told the monks it portended a court bereavement before year's end.

sentences.chinese: 」既而勒果死。
sentences.literal: " Before long Le indeed died.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Le soon followed.

sentences.chinese: 及季龍僭位，遷都於鄴，傾心事澄，有重於勒。
sentences.literal: When Jilong usurped the throne, he moved the capital to Ye and poured his heart into Cheng—more heavily than Le had.
sentences.idiomatic: After Shi Hu (Shi Jilong) seized the throne and shifted the seat to Ye, he lavished attention on Fotucheng beyond even Shi Le's devotion.

sentences.chinese: 下書衣澄以綾錦，乘以雕輦，朝會之日，引之升殿，常侍以下悉助舉輿，太子諸公扶翼而上，主者唱大和尚，眾坐皆起，以彰其尊。
sentences.literal: He issued an edict to clothe Cheng in damask and brocade, to mount him on an engraved palanquin; on court-conference days he led him up the hall—below regular attendant rank all helped lift the litter, while the heir apparent and dukes steadied him from the sides; the herald cried "Great Monk," every seated man rose, thereby displaying his honor.
sentences.idiomatic: Edicts robed the monk in silk, gave him a carved litter, and on audience days convoked him to the dais with ministers hoisting his chair and princes flanking him while criers hailed the Great Monk so that every official stood.

sentences.chinese: 又使司空李農旦夕親問，其太子諸公五日一朝，尊敬莫與為比。
sentences.literal: He also had Minister of Works Li Nong inquire morning and evening in person; his heir apparent and dukes attended audience every five days—none matched such reverence.
sentences.idiomatic: Minister of Works Li Nong attended him daily, while the heir and nobles presented themselves every fifth day—no one else enjoyed such deference.

sentences.chinese: 支道林在京師，聞澄與諸石遊，乃曰：「澄公其以季龍為海鷗鳥也。
sentences.literal: Zhi Daolin was in the capital; hearing that Cheng consorted with the various Shi, he said, "Master Cheng surely takes Jilong for a sea-gull bird."
sentences.idiomatic: Zhi Daolin in the capital, learning that Fotucheng walked among the Shi clan, remarked that the master must treat Shi Hu as the heedless gull of the fable.

sentences.chinese: 百姓因澄故多奉佛，皆營造寺廟，相競出家，真偽混淆，多生愆過。
sentences.literal: Because of Cheng the hundred surnames for the most part embraced Buddhism, all building temples, vying to leave home—true and false mingled, and very many faults arose.
sentences.idiomatic: On his account the populace turned fervently Buddhist, racing to found cloisters and tonsure until authentic practice blurred with sham and abuses multiplied.

sentences.chinese: 季龍下書料簡，其著作郎王度奏曰：「佛，外國之神，非諸華所應祠奉。
sentences.literal: Jilong issued an edict to examine and sort; his editorial director Wang Du memorialized, "The Buddha is a god of foreign lands—not what the Hua Xia ought to worship."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu ordered a review; Editorial Director Wang Du argued that the Buddha was a foreign deity unfit for Chinese state cult.

sentences.chinese: 漢代初傳其道，惟聽西域人得立寺都邑，以奉其神，漢人皆不出家。
sentences.literal: When the Han first transmitted his way, only Western Regions men were permitted to erect temples in the capitals to serve their god; Han men none left home.
sentences.idiomatic: At the Han introduction only Westerners could build urban monasteries, while native Chinese were barred from ordination.

sentences.chinese: 魏承漢制，亦循前軌。
sentences.literal: Wei inherited Han institutions and likewise followed the former track.
sentences.idiomatic: Wei continued Han precedent on the same footing.

sentences.chinese: 今可斷趙人悉不聽詣寺燒香禮拜，以遵典禮，其百辟卿士下逮眾隸，例皆禁之，其有犯者，與淫祀同罪。
sentences.literal: Now we may cut off Zhao people entirely from hearing them go to temples to burn incense and bow in worship, thereby observing canonical rites—from the hundred ministers and gentlemen down to the mass of bond servants, by rule all forbid it; those who violate shall share the guilt of illicit sacrifice.
sentences.idiomatic: He urged that Zhao subjects be forbidden temples, incense, and prostration to honor classical rites, extending the ban from high ministers to common laborers on pain of illicit-cult penalties.

sentences.chinese: 其趙人為沙門者，還服百姓。
sentences.literal: Those Zhao people who are shramanas—return them to commoner garb.
sentences.idiomatic: Any Zhao monk should be laicized.

sentences.chinese: 」朝士多同度所奏。
sentences.literal: " Court gentlemen for the most part concurred with Du's memorial.
sentences.idiomatic: Most courtiers sided with Wang Du.

sentences.chinese: 季龍以澄故，下書曰：「朕出自邊戎，忝君諸夏，至於饗祀，應從本俗。
sentences.literal: Jilong, because of Cheng, issued an edict saying, "We issue from border barbarians and disgracefully rule the Hua Xia; as to feasting sacrifice, we ought to follow our native customs.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet Shi Hu, for Fotucheng's sake, proclaimed his barbarian origins and insisted ancestral rites follow steppe custom.

sentences.chinese: 佛是戎神，所應兼奉，其夷趙百姓有樂事佛者，特聽之。」
sentences.literal: The Buddha is a barbarian god whom one ought jointly to serve; among barbarian and Zhao commoners who delight in serving the Buddha, we specially permit it."
sentences.idiomatic: The Buddha, he wrote, was a frontier deity worthy of joint worship, and any Zhao or tribesman who wished to serve him might do so.

sentences.chinese: 澄時止鄴城寺中，弟子遍于郡國。
sentences.literal: Cheng at the time lodged in Ye's monastery; disciples filled every commandery and state.
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng resided in the Ye temple while disciples spread through every province.

sentences.chinese: 嘗遣弟子法常北至襄國，弟子法佐從襄國還，相遇于梁基城下，對車夜談，言及和尚，比旦各去。
sentences.literal: Once he sent disciple Fachang north to Xiangguo; disciple Fazuo returned from Xiangguo; they met beneath Liangji city's wall, faced their carts and talked through the night, speaking of the monk; at dawn each departed.
sentences.idiomatic: He once dispatched Fachang north to Xiangguo while Fazuo returned south; the two met below Liangji, spoke in their carriages until dawn of their master, then parted.

sentences.chinese: 佐始入，澄逆笑曰：「昨夜爾與法常交車共說汝師邪？
sentences.literal: When Zuo had just entered, Cheng greeted him laughing, "Last night did you and Fachang halt carts together and speak of your teacher?"
sentences.idiomatic: As Fazuo entered, Fotucheng laughed that he had overheard their midnight colloquy about him.

sentences.chinese: 」佐愕然愧懺。
sentences.literal: " Zuo was stunned and ashamed in repentance.
sentences.idiomatic: Fazuo froze, then blushed with contrition.

sentences.chinese: 於是國人每相語：「莫起噁心，和尚知汝。
sentences.literal: From this the people whenever they spoke to each other said, "Do not harbor evil intent—the monk knows you.
sentences.idiomatic: Henceforth folk whispered that no ill thought escaped the monk's ken.

sentences.chinese: 」及澄之所在，無敢向其方面涕唾者。
sentences.literal: " Wherever Cheng dwelt, none dared toward his direction spit or weep.
sentences.idiomatic: None dared face his quarters to spit or weep.

sentences.chinese: 季龍太子邃有二字，在襄國，澄語邃曰：「小阿彌比當得疾，可往看之。
sentences.literal: Jilong's heir Sui had two sons in Xiangguo; Cheng told Sui, "Little Amita presently will fall ill—you may go look on him.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu's heir Shi Sui had two boys in Xiangguo; Fotucheng warned him the younger would sicken and bade him visit.

sentences.chinese: 」邃即馳信往視，果已得疾。
sentences.literal: " Sui immediately galloped a messenger to look; indeed he had already fallen ill.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Sui sent riders at once and found the child already stricken.

sentences.chinese: 太醫殷騰及外國道士自言能療之。
sentences.literal: Court physician Yin Teng and foreign Daoists declared themselves able to cure it.
sentences.idiomatic: Palace physician Yin Teng and foreign adepts claimed they could heal him.

sentences.chinese: 澄告弟子法牙曰：「正使聖人復出，不愈此疾，況此等乎！
sentences.literal: Cheng told disciple Faya, "Even if a sage again appeared, he would not cure this illness—how much less these!"
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng told Faya that neither sages nor charlatans could save the boy.

sentences.chinese: 」後三日果死。
sentences.literal: " After three days he indeed died.
sentences.idiomatic: Three days later the child was dead.

sentences.chinese: 邃將圖為逆，謂內豎曰：「和尚神通，儻發吾謀。
sentences.literal: Sui was about to plot treason; he told the inner attendants, "The monk has divine penetration—if he divulges my plan..."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Sui plotted revolt and muttered to eunuchs that Fotucheng's clairvoyance might expose him.

sentences.chinese: 明日來者，當先除之。
sentences.literal: " Those who come tomorrow—you should first eliminate them."
sentences.idiomatic: He ordered tomorrow's visitors killed beforehand.

sentences.chinese: 」澄月望將入覲季龍，謂弟子僧慧曰：「昨夜天神呼我曰：'明日若入，還勿過人。
sentences.literal: " Cheng on the full moon was about to enter audience with Jilong; he told disciple Seng Hui, "Last night a heavenly deity called me saying, 'If tomorrow you enter, again do not pass others.'"
sentences.idiomatic: On the day of audience Fotucheng warned Seng Hui that a spirit had forbidden him to "pass others" inside the palace.

sentences.chinese: 」我儻有所過，汝當止我。
sentences.literal: " If I perhaps pass someone, you ought to stop me.
sentences.idiomatic: If he should cross someone's path, the disciple must check him.

sentences.chinese: 」澄常入，必過邃。
sentences.literal: " Cheng whenever he entered invariably passed Sui.
sentences.idiomatic: His usual route always crossed Shi Sui's quarters.

sentences.chinese: 邃知澄入，要侯甚苦。
sentences.literal: Sui knew Cheng would enter and waited in ambush with bitter urgency.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Sui lay in desperate wait along that corridor.

sentences.chinese: 澄將上南台，僧慧引衣，澄曰：「事不得止。
sentences.literal: Cheng was about to ascend the south terrace; Seng Hui pulled his robe; Cheng said, "The affair cannot be stopped.
sentences.idiomatic: As he climbed the south terrace Seng Hui tugged his robe, but Fotucheng said the summons could not be refused.

sentences.chinese: 」坐未安便起，邃固留不住，所謀遂差。
sentences.literal: " Before he was seated securely he rose; Sui firmly could not detain him—the plot therefore missed.
sentences.idiomatic: He barely sat down, then rose and slipped Shi Sui's grasp, foiling the ambush.

sentences.chinese: 還寺，歎曰：「太子作亂，其形將成，欲言難言，欲忍難忍。
sentences.literal: Returning to the monastery he sighed, "The heir is raising rebellion—its form is about to complete; to speak is hard, to endure is hard."
sentences.idiomatic: Back at the cloister he groaned that the heir's mutiny was ripening yet could neither be told outright nor silently borne.

sentences.chinese: 」乃因事從容箴季龍，季龍終不能解。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon by affairs he leisurely admonished Jilong; Jilong to the end could not understand.
sentences.idiomatic: He circled the warning obliquely, but Shi Hu never grasped it.

sentences.chinese: 俄而事發，方悟澄言。
sentences.literal: Before long the affair broke out; then he understood Cheng's words.
sentences.idiomatic: When the plot erupted, Shi Hu finally saw his meaning.

sentences.chinese: 後郭黑略將兵征長安北山羌，墮羌伏中。
sentences.literal: Later Guo Heilüe led troops to campaign against the northern-shan Qiang of Chang'an and fell into a Qiang ambush.
sentences.idiomatic: Later Guo Heilüe campaigned against the northern-shan Qiang near Chang'an and walked into an ambush.

sentences.chinese: 時澄在堂上坐，慘然改容曰：「郭公今有厄。
sentences.literal: At the time Cheng sat in the hall; grimly he changed countenance saying, "Lord Guo now has calamity.
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng, seated in the refectory, blanched and cried that Guo Heilüe was in mortal peril.

sentences.chinese: 」乃唱云：「眾僧祝願。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he intoned, "All monks pray blessing."
sentences.idiomatic: He called for the community to pray.

sentences.chinese: 」澄又自祝願。
sentences.literal: " Cheng again personally prayed blessing.
sentences.idiomatic: Then he prayed himself.

sentences.chinese: 須臾，更曰：若東南出者活，余向者則困。
sentences.literal: After a moment he changed again saying, "If one exits southeast he lives; if toward the remaining directions then peril.
sentences.idiomatic: Moments later he amended the omen: escape southeast meant life; other headings meant doom.

sentences.chinese: 」復更祝願。
sentences.literal: " Again he changed praying blessing.
sentences.idiomatic: He prayed again.

sentences.chinese: 有頃，曰：「脫矣。
sentences.literal: After a moment he said, "He has escaped."
sentences.idiomatic: Soon he announced deliverance.

sentences.chinese: 」後月餘，黑略還，自說墜羌圍中，東南走，馬乏，正遇帳下人，推馬與之曰：「公乘此馬，小人乘公馬，濟與不濟，命也。
sentences.literal: " After more than a month Heilüe returned; himself narrated that he fell within the Qiang encirclement, fled southeast, horses exhausted, just then met a man of his tent who pushed a horse to him saying, "My lord ride this horse; your servant rides my lord's horse—whether we ford or not is fate."
sentences.idiomatic: A month later Guo Heilüe returned, telling how he broke southeast, foundered, and a retainer swapped mounts, saying survival was heaven's whim.

sentences.chinese: 」略得其馬，故獲免。
sentences.literal: " Heilüe obtained that horse; therefore he obtained escape.
sentences.idiomatic: That remount won him his life.

sentences.chinese: 推檢時日，正是澄祝願時也。
sentences.literal: Checking the times and days, it was exactly when Cheng prayed blessing.
sentences.idiomatic: The timestamps matched Fotucheng's prayers exactly.

sentences.chinese: 時天旱，季龍遣其太子詣臨漳西滏口祈雨，久而不降，乃令澄自行，即有白龍二頭降於祠所，其日大雨方數千里。
sentences.literal: At the time heaven was drought; Jilong sent his heir to Fukou west of Linzhang to pray for rain; long it did not descend; then he ordered Cheng himself to go—immediately there were two white dragons that descended at the shrine site; that day great rain fell across several thousand li.
sentences.idiomatic: During a drought Shi Hu first sent the heir to pray at Fukou west of Linzhang, then Fotucheng himself; two white dragons alighted on the altar and rain swept thousands of li.

sentences.chinese: 澄嘗遣弟子向西域市香，既行，澄告余弟子曰：「掌中見買香弟子在某處被劫垂死。
sentences.literal: Cheng once sent disciples to the Western Regions to market incense; after they had gone, Cheng told the remaining disciples, "In my palm I see the incense-buying disciple at such-and-such a place being robbed and on the verge of death."
sentences.idiomatic: When monks went west for incense, Fotucheng told those behind that vision showed the buyer ambushed and dying.

sentences.chinese: 」因燒香祝願，遙救護之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he burned incense, prayed blessing, and from afar rescued and protected him.
sentences.idiomatic: He burned incense and sent a distant deliverance.

sentences.chinese: 弟子後還，雲某月某日某處為賊所劫，垂當見殺，忽聞香氣，賊無故自驚曰：「救兵已至。
sentences.literal: The disciple afterward returned, saying on such month such day at such-and-such a place he was robbed by bandits; about to be killed, suddenly he smelled incense fragrance; the bandits without cause themselves startled said, "Relief troops have already arrived."
sentences.idiomatic: The monk returned reporting that robbers had stayed his execution until they smelled incense and fled, crying that reinforcements had come.

sentences.chinese: 」棄之而走。
sentences.literal: " They abandoned him and ran.
sentences.idiomatic: They dropped him and bolted.

sentences.chinese: 黃河中舊不生黿，時有得者，以獻季龍。
sentences.literal: In the Yellow River of old soft-shelled turtles were not born; at the time there was one obtained and presented to Jilong.
sentences.idiomatic: Yellow River turtles were unheard of until one was caught and sent to Shi Hu.

sentences.chinese: 澄見而之曰：「桓溫入河，其不久乎！
sentences.literal: Cheng seeing it said to him, "Huan Wen enters the river—will it not be soon!"
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng declared the omen meant Huan Wen would soon ford the Yellow River.

sentences.chinese: 」溫字元子，後果如其言也。
sentences.literal: " Wen's style was Yuanzi; afterward it indeed was as his words.
sentences.idiomatic: Huan Wen, styled Yuanzi, did exactly as he foretold.

sentences.chinese: 季龍嘗晝寢，夢見群羊負魚從東北來，寤以訪澄。
sentences.literal: Jilong once napped by day and dreamed a flock of sheep bearing fish came from the northeast; waking he consulted Cheng.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu dreamed sheep laden with fish from the northeast and asked Fotucheng on waking.

sentences.chinese: 澄曰：「不祥也，鮮卑其有中原乎！
sentences.literal: Cheng said, "It is inauspicious—the Xianbei will possess the Central Plain!"
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng called it ill-omened: the Xianbei would take the heartland.

sentences.chinese: 」後亦皆驗。
sentences.literal: " Later too all were verified.
sentences.idiomatic: Later events bore him out.

sentences.chinese: 澄嘗與季龍升中台，澄忽驚曰：「變，變，幽州當火災。
sentences.literal: Cheng once with Jilong ascended the middle terrace; Cheng suddenly startled said, "Change, change—Youzhou will have a fire disaster."
sentences.idiomatic: On the central tower he suddenly cried that Youzhou faced a great blaze.

sentences.chinese: 」乃取酒噀之，久而笑曰：「救已得矣。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he took wine and sprayed it; after a long while he laughed saying, "The rescue has already been obtained."
sentences.idiomatic: He spat wine into the air, then laughed that the danger was averted.

sentences.chinese: 」季龍遣驗幽州，雲爾日火從四門起，西南有黑雲來，驟雨滅之，雨亦頗有酒氣。
sentences.literal: " Jilong sent to verify Youzhou; they reported that day fire rose from the four gates; from the southwest there came black clouds; sudden rain extinguished it; the rain too rather had the smell of wine.
sentences.idiomatic: Inspectors reported flames bursting from Youzhou's gates until black clouds and a reeking downpour—almost vinous—doused them.

sentences.chinese: 石宣將殺石韜，宣先到寺與澄同坐，浮屠一鈴獨鳴，澄謂曰：「解鈴音乎？
sentences.literal: Shi Xuan was about to kill Shi Tao; Xuan first arrived at the temple and sat together with Cheng; one pagoda bell alone rang; Cheng told him, "Do you understand the bell's sound?"
sentences.idiomatic: Before Shi Xuan murdered Shi Tao he sat with Fotucheng while a lone bell tolled; the monk asked if he grasped its message.

sentences.chinese: 鈴雲鬍子洛度。
sentences.literal: The bell declares: the bearded man crosses the river.
sentences.idiomatic: The bell, he said, meant "the bearded man fords the river"—a Jie gloss on the plot.

sentences.chinese: 」宣變色曰：「是何言歟？
sentences.literal: " Xuan changed color saying, "What sort of talk is this!"
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Xuan flushed and demanded what he meant.

sentences.chinese: 」澄謬曰：「老胡為道，不能山居無言，重茵美服，豈非洛度乎！
sentences.literal: " Cheng falsely said, "The old barbarian practices the Way—unable to dwell in mountains in silence, layered mats and fine robes—is that not crossing the river!"
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng feigned to mock his own luxury as a monk who could not keep mountain silence.

sentences.chinese: 」石韜後至，澄孰視良久。
sentences.literal: " Shi Tao afterward arrived; Cheng stared fixedly a long while.
sentences.idiomatic: When Shi Tao entered, Fotucheng studied him at length.

sentences.chinese: 韜懼而問澄，澄曰：「怪公血臭，故相視耳。
sentences.literal: Tao feared and asked Cheng; Cheng said, "I marveled that lord's blood stank—therefore I gazed."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Tao quailed; Fotucheng said only that he smelled blood on him.

sentences.chinese: 」季龍夢龍飛西南，自天而落，旦而問澄，澄曰：「禍將作矣，宜父子慈和，深以慎之。
sentences.literal: " Jilong dreamed a dragon flew southwest, from heaven and fell; at dawn he asked Cheng; Cheng said, "Disaster is about to arise—you ought to be father-son kind and harmonious, deeply thereby be cautious."
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu dreamed a dragon plummet from the sky; Fotucheng warned of coming woe and urged father-son harmony.

sentences.chinese: 」季龍引澄入東閣，與其後杜氏問訊之。
sentences.literal: " Jilong led Cheng into the east pavilion and with his empress Du questioned him.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu brought him to the east gallery for Empress Du to question.

sentences.chinese: 澄曰：「脅下有賊，不出十日，自浮圖以西，此殿以東，當有血流，慎勿東也。
sentences.literal: Cheng said, "Beneath the ribs there is a bandit—within ten days, from west of the pagoda to east of this hall, there ought to be flowing blood—be careful not to go east."
sentences.idiomatic: He warned of assassins within ten days, blood west of the stupa and east of the hall, and bade them shun the eastern precincts.

sentences.chinese: 」杜後曰：「和尚耄邪！
sentences.literal: " Empress Du said, "Monk, are you senile!"
sentences.idiomatic: Empress Du sneered that the monk was senile.

sentences.chinese: 何處有賊？
sentences.literal: " Where would there be bandits?"
sentences.idiomatic: She asked where brigands could hide.

sentences.chinese: 」澄即易語云：「六情所受，皆悉是賊。
sentences.literal: " Cheng immediately changed words saying, "The six emotions' receipts—all are entirely bandits.
sentences.idiomatic: Fotucheng pivoted, saying every passion was a robber of the mind.

sentences.chinese: 老自應耄，但使少者不昏即好耳。
sentences.literal: The old naturally ought to be senile—but let it suffice that the young not be muddled."
sentences.idiomatic: He granted his own dotage if only the young stayed clear-headed.

sentences.chinese: 」遂便寓言，不復彰的。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he then spoke in allegory, no longer making it explicit.
sentences.idiomatic: He dropped explicit prophecy and spoke in parables.

sentences.chinese: 後二日，宣果遣人害韜於佛寺中，欲因季龍臨喪殺之。
sentences.literal: After two days Xuan indeed sent men to harm Tao inside a Buddhist temple, wishing by Jilong's coming to the funeral to kill him.
sentences.idiomatic: Two days later Shi Xuan had Shi Tao murdered in a monastery, planning to strike Shi Hu at the obsequies.

sentences.chinese: 季龍以澄先誡，故獲免。
sentences.literal: Jilong because Cheng had beforehand warned therefore obtained escape.
sentences.idiomatic: Forewarned by Fotucheng, Shi Hu escaped the trap.

sentences.chinese: 及宣被收，澄諫季龍曰：「皆陛下之子也，何為重禍邪！
sentences.literal: When Xuan was arrested, Cheng remonstrated Jilong saying, "They are all Your Majesty's sons—why double the calamity!"
sentences.idiomatic: When Shi Xuan was seized, Fotucheng begged Shi Hu not to compound the tragedy among his sons.

sentences.chinese: 陛下若含怒加慈者，尚有六十餘歲。
sentences.literal: If Your Majesty will contain wrath and add kindness, still there are more than sixty years.
sentences.idiomatic: Mercy, he said, could yet extend Shi Hu's life sixty-some years.

sentences.chinese: 如必誅之，宣當為彗星下掃鄴宮。
sentences.literal: If you must execute him, Xuan ought to become a broom-comet sweeping down the Ye palace.
sentences.idiomatic: If Shi Xuan were put to death, a comet would scour the Ye palaces—so he warned.

sentences.chinese: 」季龍不從。
sentences.literal: " Jilong did not follow.
sentences.idiomatic: Shi Hu refused the plea.

sentences.chinese: 後月餘，有一妖馬，髦尾皆有燒狀，入中陽門，出顯陽門，東首東宮，皆不得入，走向東北，俄爾不見。
sentences.literal: After more than a month there was one demon horse—mane and tail both had scorched marks—it entered Zhongyang Gate, exited Xianyang Gate, turned east toward the Eastern Palace, all could not enter, ran toward the northeast, before long disappeared.
sentences.idiomatic: A month later a spectral horse with burnt mane and tail galloped from Zhongyang to Xianyang gate, wheeled toward the Eastern Palace yet could not enter, then fled northeast and vanished.
